correctness.rationale: For every pair of binary sequences, the difference of two coordinate truncations sends the corresponding molecule to a four-atom signed measure. The two-by-two transportation formula gives the exact value min(a+b,2p+h), where p is weighted prefix disagreement, h block disagreement, and a,b individual block masses. This yields the universal ratio bound max(1,2 min(1,B/a_n)), attained by a block-only molecule and by a minimum-prefix-weight rectangle whose two block sequences are all ones. It also covers infinite upper endpoints because summability keeps all distances finite. Norm-one ranks and strong convergence of the coordinate projections follow from 1-Lipschitz retractions and uniform tail decay. check_intervals.py independently maximizes every finite molecule image via dual Lipschitz LP and matches all 48 finite-cube interval cases to 8.9e-16. Only the analytic proof establishes all infinite cases.

originality.rationale: The exact formula is a complete weighted interval-projection norm profile, not merely a metric approximation property or existence of a Schauder decomposition. The 2020 compact-group theorem already covers MAP here; the 2012 interpolation-based decomposition covers free spaces over ambient l1, not this explicit interval projection norm. The inspected Cantor metric paper and group projection article do not imply the quantitative threshold, and targeted searches located no equivalent result. A previously unnoticed application of four-point transport in unindexed literature remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: An explicitly specified monotone finite-dimensional Schauder decomposition is a natural tool for the approximation geometry of Cantor Lipschitz-free spaces. The exact interval norm of every consecutive block is an intrinsic, nontrivial operator invariant of that chosen decomposition. Its sharp 1-versus-2 behavior is controlled by the ratio of the entire interval mass to the minimum previously retained coordinate weight, yielding a complete bimonotonicity classification. The geometric example alpha_j=r^j has individual block contractivity up to r=1/2 but bimonotonicity only up to r=1/3, a substantive structural distinction not determined by qualitative MAP, code correctness or trivial norm estimates.
